body: Etrian Odyssey III: The Drowned City is Atlus's Nintendo DS dungeon role-playing game about a player-created guild investigating the labyrinth beneath Armoroad. The first-person journey and hand-drawn touchscreen map return, now joined by seafaring exploration and a new set of character classes. A party of up to five adventurers represents a larger guild whose members can be changed in town. The structure keeps preparation close to discovery: the next expedition begins with a choice of people and supplies as well as a destination on the map.

The new classes provide different skills, equipment and statistics, while subclassing later allows most characters to combine part of another role with their own. Those choices affect what the party can accomplish during encounters and how safely it can sustain an expedition. A guild can retain more members than it takes into the labyrinth, allowing another group to be prepared for a different purpose. The hand-drawn record of the route is shared, but the group following it can change as the player understands what lies farther below.

The mapping tools include symbols for currents, landmarks and notes, supporting the game's interest in routes as well as rooms. Recording what has been found makes a future journey more predictable, while another unexamined direction keeps the larger area uncertain. The combination gives the series' patient exploration another setting beyond its familiar corridors. Etrian Odyssey III treats both the guild and its map as things built through play. Each expedition can return with a stronger character, a better plan and a small piece of information that makes the next departure possible.
